intended_object: For an extension of number fields L/K and a finite set S of finite primes of K, this is the Gal(L/K)-equivariant valuation map from the S-units of L to the free ℤ-module on the primes of L above S, u ↦ (v_w(u))_w. It is a morphism of ℤ[G]-modules and is used in the Herbrand quotient computation for idele classes (Milne, CFT VII §3). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The source is `sUnitsRep L S`, the S_L-units of L (S_L = primes above S) with their Galois action. The target is the permutation representation ℤ[S_L], with Aut(L/K) permuting the primes above S. The underlying map composes `Set.unitValuation`, which is u ↦ (w.valuationOfNeZero u)_w, with some linear equivalences: Additive of functions to Multiplicative ℤ ≅ functions to ℤ ≅ finitely supported functions ≅ MonoidAlgebra. Together these turn the valuations into the integer coefficient vector. The equivariance proof uses v_{σw}(σu) = v_w(u), which is the standard identity.

One remark on sign. Mathlib's `valuationOfNeZero` sends a uniformizer to `ofAdd (-1)`, so each coefficient is −ord_w(u) rather than ord_w(u). The docstring only says the valuation is "written additively", which matches Mathlib's convention. Also, negation is a G-equivariant automorphism of ℤ[S_L], so the kernel, the image index and the equivariance are the same either way. I count this as a convention, not an error.

Generality: the object is inherently about number fields, the Galois group Aut(L/K) and the finite set of primes above S. The underlying general Dedekind-domain valuation map (`Set.unitValuation`) is already stated generally elsewhere in the library. Mathlib has no equivariant version of this map, so nothing is being restated more narrowly.
